England striker Ivan Toney pleads not guilty to assault charge, trial set for 2028
 The Al-Ahli forward appeared at Southwark Crown Court over an alleged nightclub assault in London, with his trial provisionally scheduled during Euro 2028.
 Updated : Oct 29, 2026 20:05 IST , CHENNAI - 2 MINS READ

 Ivan Toney pleaded not guilty to an assault charge on Thursday, with his trial scheduled for June 2028.
 | Photo Credit: REUTERS
 Ivan Toney pleaded not guilty to an assault charge on Thursday, with his trial scheduled for June 2028.
 | Photo Credit: REUTERS
 England international Ivan Toney pleaded not guilty to an assault charge at Southwark Crown Court in London on Thursday, with his trial provisionally scheduled for June 12, 2028.
 The 30-year-old striker, who plays for Saudi Arabian club Al-Ahli, is accused of headbutting and punching a man following an altercation at a nightclub on Wardour Street in London on December 6, 2025.
 Toney appeared before Judge Christopher Hehir during a five-minute hearing and denied a charge of assault occasioning actual bodily harm, according to Britain’s Press Association news agency.
 ALSO READ | England striker Ivan Toney charged with assault at London nightclub 
 The judge apologised for the lengthy delay in scheduling the trial, citing a significant backlog of cases in the Crown Courts.
 The trial date falls during the 2028 European Championship, which will take place from June 9 to July 9 across England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
 Toney was released on unconditional bail following the hearing.
 The England forward began his professional career with Northampton Town and later played for Newcastle United and Peterborough United before joining Brentford in 2020. He moved to Al-Ahli in 2024.
 Toney has made 10 appearances for England, scoring once, and was part of the national squad at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
 ( With inputs from AP ).
